name: Chest pain, mild persisting
transcript:
You said you have chest pain — thank you. First, is the person conscious and breathing normally and able to respond if you call to them?

Please choose one:
- Yes — conscious, breathing normally and responding
- Cardiac arrest
- Not breathing
- Unresponsive / not responding to call
- Confused, agitated or disoriented
- Altered mental state / not fully conscious
- Obvious neurological deficit
Yes — conscious, breathing normally and responding.
Thanks — can I ask your age in years?

Thanks — you’re 30 and have chest pain. Next: how is the breathing? Please choose one answer:

- Breathing normally
- Severe respiratory distress
- Abnormal breathing sounds
- Excessive work of breathing with sweating
- Cannot speak / one-word replies only
- Short phrases only
- Difficulty to breathe
- Agitated or anxious because of breathing difficulty
- Wheeze or expiratory rhonchi with airway intact

Thanks — noted you’re breathing normally. Next: Is there any bleeding, major trauma, or severe injury?

Please choose one:
- No bleeding or minimal bleeding
- Arterial limb bleeding
- Active uncontrolled bleeding
- Massive vaginal bleeding
- Severe facial injury
- Severe pelvic injury
- Major trauma with shock
- Pale, bluish (cyanosed) skin with cold hands/feet
- Active vomiting or coughing of blood
- Bleeding from fractures, dislocations, joints or wounds
- Heavy periods (menorrhagia)
- ENT (nose/ear/throat) bleeding
- Expanding haematoma (swelling with bleeding under the skin)
- Known bleeding disorder

You said you have chest pain — thanks. Is there chest pain or other pain? How severe is it on a scale of 0 to 10?

Please answer one:
- Severe chest pain
- Severe pain (8-10)
- Moderate pain (4-7)
- Mild pain (1-3)
- No pain (0)

Thanks — noted mild chest pain (1–3). 

Is the person having a seizure, or unable to sit, stand, walk or communicate?

Please choose one:
- Ongoing seizures
- Cannot sit or stand unsupported
- Cannot stand or walk unsupported
- Cannot communicate
- Alert, walking and talking normally

Is your skin pale or bluish, or are your hands or feet unusually cold?

Please choose one:
- Yes
- No
- Not sure

Thanks — noted mild chest pain and breathing normal. When did the chest pain start?

Please choose one:
- New onset starting within less than 6 hours
- Started more than 6 hours ago
- Chest pain is reducing
- No further pain

Thanks — noted the pain started >6 hours ago. Quick question: are you experiencing profuse sweating alongside the chest pain?

Please answer:
- Yes
- No

Thanks — noted. Is your chest pain reducing now?

Please choose one:
- Yes — chest pain is reducing
- No — pain is the same or worse
- No further pain
No — the pain is still there and hasn't improved.

Thanks — one quick related question to finish screening.

Are you currently having heavy vaginal bleeding (soaking pads or clothes), or do you have a known bleeding disorder or take blood-thinning medicine (warfarin, DOACs, aspirin, clopidogrel)?

Please answer one:
- No to both
- Yes — heavy vaginal bleeding now
- Yes — known bleeding disorder or on blood thinners
- Not sure

Level 4 - Early Care

Level 4 - Early Care (target: under 60 minutes). Needs medical care soon: go to an Emergency Department or a walk-in / urgent-care clinic.

Key findings: persisting mild chest pain.

If you want, I can help find nearby emergency departments or urgent-care clinics — tell me your location or postcode. 

This is a preliminary screening, not a medical diagnosis. It does not replace assessment by a healthcare professional. If symptoms worsen, call 999 (112 from mobile).
